source: Dallas City Code ch. 51P, Article 562 (City Attorney's codified article, April 2026)

sections.title: Article heading
sections.text:
ARTICLE 562.

PD 562.

sections.title: Legislative History
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-562.101. LEGISLATIVE HISTORY.

PD 562 was established by Ordinance No. 24137, passed by the Dallas City Council on December 8, 1999. Ordinance No. 24137 amended Ordinance No. 19455, Chapter 51A of the Dallas City Code, as amended. Subsequently, Ordinance No. 24137 was amended by Ordinance No. 24451, passed by the Dallas City Council on November 8, 2000. (Ord. Nos. 19455; 24137; 24451; 25163)

sections.title: Property Location And Size
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-562.102. PROPERTY LOCATION AND SIZE.

PD 562 is established on property fronting on the north line of Keller Springs Road, east of the Dallas North Tollway. The size of PD 562 is approximately 63.3703 acres. (Ord. Nos. 24137; 25163)

sections.title: Definitions And Interpretations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-562.103. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS.

(a) Unless otherwise stated, the definitions and interpretations in Chapter 51A apply to this article.

(b) Unless otherwise stated, all code references are to Chapter 51A.

(c) This district is considered to be a residential zoning district. (Ord. Nos. 24137; 25163)

sections.title: Development Plan
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-562.104. DEVELOPMENT PLAN.

Use and development of the Property must comply with the development plan (Exhibit 562A). In the event of a conflict between the provisions of this article and the development plan, the provisions of this article control. (Ord. Nos. 24137; 24451; 25163)

sections.title: Construction Traffic
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-562.105. CONSTRUCTION TRAFFIC.

It is the intent of the city council to minimize construction traffic in residential neighborhoods. Therefore, issuance of any building permit on the Property is conditioned upon approval of a construction traffic management plan by the building official showing that the proposed routes for construction traffic will not go through minor residential streets. A violation of the construction management plan is a violation of this article and may result in issuance of citations or a stop-work order. (Ord. Nos. 24137; 25163)

sections.title: Main Uses Permitted
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-562.106. MAIN USES PERMITTED.

(a) Institutional and community service uses.

-- Church.

(b) Miscellaneous uses.

-- Temporary construction or sales office.

(c) Recreation uses.

-- Private recreation center, club, or area (a maximum of 1,800 square feet and located as shown on the development plan).

(d) Residential uses.

-- Handicapped group dwelling unit. [SUP required if spacing component of Section 51A-4.209(3.1) is not met.] -- Single family.

(e) Transportation uses.

-- Private street or alley.

(f) Utility and public service uses.

-- Local utilities. (Ord. Nos. 24451; 25163)

sections.title: Accessory Uses
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-562.107. ACCESSORY USES.

(a) As a general rule, an accessory use is permitted in any district in which the main use is permitted. Some specific types of accessory uses, however, due to their unique nature, are subject to additional regulations in Section 51A-4.217. For more information regarding accessory uses, consult Section 51A-4.217.

(b) The following accessory uses are not permitted in this district:

-- Accessory helistop. -- Accessory medical/infectious waste incinerator. -- Accessory outside display of merchandise. -- Accessory outside sales. -- Accessory pathological waste incinerator. -- Private stable. (Ord. Nos. 24137; 25163)

sections.title: Yard, Lot, And Space Regulations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-562.108. YARD, LOT, AND SPACE REGULATIONS.

(a) Front yard.

(1) Tracts 1, 3, and 4. Minimum front yard is five feet.

(2) Tract 2. Minimum front yard is 20 feet.

(b) Side yard.

(1) Tracts 1, 3, and 4. The side yard must consist of a minimum of one foot on one side of each platted lot and a minimum of three feet on the opposite side of each platted lot.

(2) Tract 2. Minimum side yard is six feet.

(c) Rear yard.

(1) Tracts 1, 2, and 3. Minimum rear yard is 6 feet, except as shown on the development plan where indicating a minimum rear yard of 25 feet.

(2) Tract 4. Minimum rear yard is five feet.

(3) All tracts. For all Tracts, the following are permitted to be located in the required rear yard: swimming pool (private), jacuzzi, spa, gazebo, bathhouse/pool house, tennis court, basketball court, arbor, trellis, and decks.

(d) Setbacks for common area or open space.

(1) Except as provided below, for any permitted structure located in a common area or open space, there is no required setback.

(2) For a private recreation center, club, or area, minimum setbacks are as shown on the development plan.

(e) Density.

(1) Tract 1. Maximum number of dwelling units is 32.

(2) Tract 2. Maximum number of dwelling units is 54.

(3) Tract 3. Maximum number of dwelling units is 18.

(4) Tract 4. Maximum number of dwelling units is nine.

(f) Height. For all tracts, maximum structure height is 36 feet.

(g) Lot coverage.

(1) Tracts 1, 3, and 4. Maximum lot coverage is 80 percent for residential structures and 25 percent for nonresidential structures.

(2) Tract 2.

(A) Except as provided below, maximum lot coverage is 50 percent for residential structures and 25 percent for nonresidential structures.

(B) For a private recreation center, club, or area, maximum lot coverage is as shown on the development plan.

(h) Lot size.

(1) Tracts 1, 3, and 4. Minimum lot size for residential uses is 5,000 square feet.

(2) Tract 2. Minimum lot size for residential uses is 15,000 square feet. (Ord. Nos. 24451; 25163

sections.title: Off-Street Parking And Loading
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-562.109. OFF-STREET PARKING AND LOADING.

(a) Except as provided below, for all other permitted uses, consult the use regulations contained in Division 51A-4.200 for the specific off-street parking and loading requirements for each use. Consult Division 51A-4.300 for information regarding off-street parking and loading generally.

(b) For a private recreation center, club, or area, off-street parking must be provided and located as shown on the development plan. For purposes of the section, screening of off-street parking is not required. (Ord. Nos. 24451; 25163)

sections.title: Environmental Performance Standards
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-562.110. ENVIRONMENTAL PERFORMANCE STANDARDS.

See Article VI. (Ord. Nos. 24137; 25163)

sections.title: Electrical Service For Single Family Uses
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-562.111. ELECTRICAL SERVICE FOR SINGLE FAMILY USES.

(a) In this planned development district, a lot for a single family use may be supplied by not more than one electrical utility service, and metered by not more than one electrical meter.

(b) The board of adjustment may grant a special exception to authorize more than one electrical utility service and more than one electrical meter on a lot in this planned development district when, in the opinion of the board, the special exception will:

(1) not be contrary to the public interest;

(2) not adversely affect neighboring properties; and

(3) not be used to conduct a use not permitted in this planned development district. (Ord. Nos. 24137; 25163)

sections.title: Access
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-562.112. ACCESS.

(a) Ingress and egress must be provided as shown on the development plan.

(b) Private street widths must have a minimum of 53 feet of right-of-way with a minimum of 33 feet of pavement width face-to-face for Street A, Street B, and Street C, as indicated on Exhibit 562B.

(c) Private street widths must have a minimum of 50 feet of right-of-way with a minimum of 26 feet of pavement width face-to-face for Street D, Street E, and Street F as indicated on Exhibit 562B.

(d) Ingress and egress from Westgrove Drive is prohibited. (Ord. Nos. 24137; 25163)

sections.title: Landscaping
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-562.113. LANDSCAPING.

(a) Except as provided in Subsections (b), (c), and (d), prior to the final inspection for each single family use, landscaping must be provided for each platted lot and must be provided in accordance with Article X.

(b) Trees totaling a minimum of six caliper inches must either exist or be provided for on each platted lot. Each tree that is to be counted towards the six caliper inch requirement must be at least two caliper inches. For example, a two inch caliper tree and a four inch caliper tree located on the same platted lot will satisfy the six caliper inch requirement for that platted lot.

(c) There is no minimum tree requirement for each platted lot (including no minimum for the front yard in each platted lot).

(d) Prior to the issuance of a certificate of occupancy for a private recreation center, club, or area, the following landscaping must be provided with final plant species to be approved by the building official: (1) one large tree, a minimum of three caliper inches, for each 4,000 square feet of lot area; (2) one large tree for each 50 feet of street frontage, to be located within 20 feet of the street curb; (3) a foundation planting strip as defined in Article X, except that the planting areas must be a minimum of four feet in width and must extend a minimum of 50 percent of the entire building perimeter.

(e) All plant materials must be maintained in a healthy, growing condition. (Ord. Nos. 24451; 25163)

sections.title: Tree Preservation
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-562.114. TREE PRESERVATION.

(a) Except as provided in Subsections (b) and (c), the regulations contained in Division 51A- 10.130, "Tree Preservation," apply to this planned development district.

(b) Prior to the removal of any trees from the Property, a tree survey must be completed and delivered to the building official.

(c) Tree removal applications may be approved by the building official prior to the issuance of a building permit on the Property.

(d) Mitigation of tree removal for the first 35 developed lots must be completed prior to the first of the following to occur:

(1) The 35th final building inspection for these 35 lots.

(2) Three years from the date of the issuance of the first building permit for work within these 35 lots.

(e) Mitigation of tree removal for the next 35 developed lots must be completed prior to the first of the following to occur:

(1) The 70th final building inspection for these 35 lots.

(2) Three years from the date of the issuance of the first building permit for work within these 35 lots.

(f) Mitigation of tree removal for the next 32 developed lots must be completed prior to the first of the following to occur:

(1) The 102nd final building inspection for these 32 lots.

(2) Three years from the date of the issuance of the first building permit for work within these 32 lots.

(g) Any surplus of the mitigation of tree removal that is created for the provisions of either Subsection (d) or Subsection (e) may be applied towards the replacement requirements in Subsections (e) or (f). This surplus credit, which must be approved by the city arborist, may only be applied once toward the Property. (Ord. Nos. 24137; 25163)

sections.title: Fences, Walls, Entryway Columns, And Gates
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-562.115. FENCES, WALLS, ENTRYWAY COLUMNS, AND GATES.

(a) Except as provided in Subsection (c), the maximum height for all fences, walls, entryway columns, and gates on the Property, excluding those that front on a public or private street or an access easement, is 10 feet.

(b) Except as provided in Subsection (c), the maximum height for all fences and walls on the Property that front a public or private street or an access easement is 12 feet. The maximum height for all entryway columns and gates on the Property that front on a public or private street or an access easement is 18 feet.

(c) Except for Lots A and B located within Tract 2, fences in front yards may not exceed four feet in height. All fences and walls on Lots A and B within Tract 2 may be built up to a maximum of 12 feet in height in the front yard. All entryway columns and gates on Lots A and B within Tract 2 may be built up to a maximum of 18 feet in height in the front yard.

(d) The visual obstruction regulations contained in Section 51A-4.602(d) apply to this planned development district. (Ord. Nos. 24137; 25163)

sections.title: Guardhouse
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-562.116. GUARDHOUSE.

A guardhouse is permitted on the Property and is limited in location to Street A as located on Exhibit 562B. The guardhouse must be located between the property line fronting Keller Springs Road and the controlled access gates, with the final location and design to be approved by the director of public works and transportation. For purposes of this provision, the yard, lot, and space regulations of this article do not apply. (Ord. Nos. 24137; 25163)

sections.title: Floodway
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-562.117. FLOODWAY.

(a) No platted lot may extend into the floodway.

(b) Any land area extending into the floodway must be dedicated as a floodway management area, floodway easement, common area, or park. (Ord. Nos. 24137; 25163)

sections.title: Homeowners’ Association
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-562.118. HOMEOWNERS’ ASSOCIATION.

Prior to final plat approval, the owner(s) of the Property must execute an instrument creating a homeowners' association for the maintenance of common areas, screening walls, landscape areas (including right-of-way landscaping areas), private streets, and for other functions. This instrument must be approved as to form by the city attorney, and filed in the Dallas County deed records. (Ord. Nos. 24137; 25163)

sections.title: Signs
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-562.119. SIGNS.

Signs must comply with the provisions for non-business zoning districts contained in Article VII. (Ord. Nos. 24137; 25163)

sections.title: Sidewalks
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-562.120. SIDEWALKS.

(a) Sidewalks and barrier-free ramps are required along the Keller Springs Road street frontage.

(b) Sidewalks and barrier-free ramps are not required for all other street frontage on the Property. (Ord. Nos. 24137; 25163)

sections.title: Traffic Signal
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-562.121. TRAFFIC SIGNAL.

The owner/developer of the Property is authorized to install, at his or her own expense, a traffic signal at the intersection of Keller Springs Road and Street A, as indicated on Exhibit 562B. The City will cooperate in the processing of plans and will not unreasonably withhold inspections, approvals, and/or related requests by the owner/developer. (Ord. Nos. 24137; 25163)

sections.title: Additional Provisions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-562.122. ADDITIONAL PROVISIONS.

(a) The Property must be properly maintained in a state of good repair and neat appearance.

(b) Development and use of the Property must comply with all federal and state laws and regulations, and with all ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. Nos. 24137; 25163; 26102)

sections.title: Compliance With Conditions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-562.123. COMPLIANCE WITH CONDITIONS.

(a) All paved areas, permanent drives, streets, and drainage structures, if any, must be constructed in accordance with standard city specifications, and completed to the satisfaction of the director of public works and transportation.

(b) The building official shall not issue a building permit or a certificate of occupancy for a use in this planned development district until there has been full compliance with this article, the Dallas Development Code, the construction codes, and all other ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. Nos. 24137; 25163; 26102)

sections.title: Zoning Map
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-562.124. ZONING MAP.

PD 562 is located on Zoning Map Nos. A-7 and B-7. (Ord. Nos. 24137; 25163)
